blocks.text: When the external conditions of temperature and pressure change, the volume of a given quantity of gas is affected; the gas laws describe the relationships between the volume of a given amount of gas and the prevailing temperature and pressure. In Boyle's and Charles's laws some variables are held constant: by Boyle's law V is proportional to 1/P when n and T are constant (1); by Charles's law V is proportional to T when n and P are constant (2); and by Avogadro's law the volume of a gas at constant temperature and pressure is directly proportional to the number of moles, V proportional to n when P and T are constant (3). If none of the variables is kept constant, the three relationships join as V proportional to nT/P, or V = constant x nT/P. The constant is R, the ideal gas constant, whose value is 0.0821 atm dm3 per K per mol. Hence V = RnT/P, that is PV = nRT (4), the ideal gas equation.
Calculation of the relative molecular mass of a gas

Equation (4) gives the relative molecular mass of a gas whose P, T, V and mass in grams are known. Putting n = m/M, where m is the mass in grams and M the molar mass, PV = mRT/M (5), and rearranging, M = mRT/PV (6). At the molecular level the molar mass is the relative molecular mass, so Mr = mRT/PV (7).

blocks.caption: Sample Problem 5.1
rows: 134 g of gas, -73 degrees C (200 K), 10 atm, 5 dm3

blocks.prompt: The volume of 21 g of a gas is 8 dm3 at -90 degrees C under 7 atm. Calculate its relative molecular mass.
blocks.explanation: T = 273 - 90 = 183 K. M = mRT / PV = (21 x 0.0821 x 183) / (7 x 8) = 315.5 / 56 = 5.6 g/mol, so the relative molecular mass is about 5.6 (close to helium's 4 given the rounding of the printed data).

items: Boyle (V proportional to 1/P), Charles (V proportional to T) and Avogadro (V proportional to n) combine into PV = nRT with R = 0.0821 atm dm3 per K per mol.
With n = m/M, the relative molecular mass is Mr = mRT / PV (Sample 5.1: 44).
